items.title: Steve Turré interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 29, 2021
items.q: And we would rehearse and get to the gigs and sometimes he wouldn’t even play what we rehearsed and he’d just start playing and we’d have to listen and go with it.

ctx.x: It is interesting that he could have been — just if he played tenor sax he would have been like a major contributor to the jazz lexicon I guess is what I’m trying to say but and of course in addition he had all that other things that he did.

You know what’s interesting? I mean to me Rahsaan is the first grand master that I’ve played with and then later on, once I came to New York I played with him again up until he passed. But he could play anything. I mean musically. Spiritual things man. And he was encouraging but at the same time he would tell you like it is and sometimes it would hurt, or sometimes it was like a slap, a wake-up. You know? Listen. All that counts. Because I remember he played the whole history of the music in the course of the…

It’s funny you mention that because I recall watching, that time I saw him, he sort of made me nervous with his horns. I’m a saxophone player too, so you know he was surrounded by his instruments and of course he was blind, so he’d be reaching all over.
